articles.title: Isolated avulsion of the short head of the biceps tendon from the coracoid insertion: A case report and narrative review of the literature.
articles.authors: Damiani L, Consigliere P, West S
articles.population: 34-year-old healthy male
articles.outcomes: Return to normal daily and sports activities at 6 months; no residual anatomical deformity; no clinically evident strength deficit
articles.take_home: This is the first reported case of an isolated short head of biceps tendon being pulled off its attachment point at the coracoid bone following an injury. Surgical repair allowed the patient to return to normal activities and sports within 6 months.

articles.title: Occult Infection Risk with Stem Retention in Revision Anatomic to Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Shenoy DA, Parsons KE, Henriquez A, Hurley ET, Leal J, Menendez ME, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing conversion from anatomic to reverse shoulder arthroplasty with stem retention using a convertible humeral component
articles.outcomes: Postoperative infection rates, reoperation for infection, intraoperative culture findings, patient-reported outcomes (SANE and ASES scores), complications
articles.take_home: Retaining the humeral stem during conversion surgery resulted in a low infection rate (3.1% requiring reoperation), but unexpectedly positive bacterial cultures were found in 14% of cases, suggesting surgeons should remain vigilant for hidden infection even when preoperative risk appears low.

articles.title: Radial Head Arthroplasty for Radial Head Fracture Is Associated with a Lower Rate of Reoperation Than Open Reduction Internal Fixation: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Carroll PJ, Chang N, Pequeno P, Nam D, Paterson JM, Sheth U
articles.study_type: Population-based cohort study using health administrative databases
articles.population: Patients aged 16 years and older in Ontario, Canada with radial head fractures treated surgically
articles.outcomes: Rate of reoperation over mean follow-up of 8-11 years. At 10 years, cumulative incidence of reoperation was 15.8% for ORIF, 10.4% for RHA and 6.5% for excision. Most common secondary procedure was hardware removal.
articles.take_home: Replacing the radial head with an artificial joint (RHA) led to fewer patients needing further surgery compared with repairing and fixing the broken bone with plates and screws (ORIF). In younger patients under 40, surgery performed overnight was linked with more reoperations.

articles.title: Differences in valgus and internal-rotation instability after sequential distal ulnar collateral ligament release: a cadaveric study using Thiel-embalmed cadavers.
articles.authors: Matsuzawa K, Edama M, Sakamoto K, Akeda M, Sakata J, Sato N
articles.population: Thiel-embalmed cadavers
articles.outcomes: Valgus instability (medial joint space) and internal rotation instability (posteromedial joint space) after sequential distal ulnar collateral ligament release
articles.take_home: When the distal ulnar collateral ligament is torn, the elbow becomes unstable in both sideways movement and internal rotation, but internal rotation instability increases more. This may explain why distal tears cause worse outcomes in overhead athletes, as increased internal rotation instability leads to the characteristic inward rotation malalignment seen clinically.

articles.title: Preoperative Pseudoparesis Is Not Associated With Inferior Outcomes After Anterior Latissimus Dorsi and Teres Major Transfer for Irreparable Anterosuperior Rotator Cuff Tears: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
articles.authors: Baek CH, Kim JG, Kim BT, Lim C, Kim SJ
articles.study_type: Retrospective comparative cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing combined anterior latissimus dorsi and teres major transfer for irreparable anterosuperior rotator cuff tears
articles.sample_size: 57 matched pairs (114 patients total; 57 with pseudoparesis, 57 without)
articles.outcomes: Clinical scores (VAS, ADLIR, Constant, UCLA, ASES), range of motion, strength, subscapularis-specific tests, tendon integrity on 2-year MRI, retear rates
articles.take_home: Patients with pseudoparesis before surgery had larger improvements in arm lifting and movement after this transfer operation, but final outcomes were similar to those without pseudoparesis. Pseudoparesis did not indicate a worse long-term result.

articles.title: Effects of Early Rehabilitation on Shoulder Joint Stiffness and Functional Recovery Following Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair.
articles.authors: Shou S, He L, Liu P, Zhi J, Xu L
articles.population: Patients who underwent arthroscopic rotator cuff repair between January 2019 and January 2023
articles.outcomes: Shoulder stiffness at 3 months (primary); Constant score, ASES score, pain (VAS), and passive forward flexion (secondary)
articles.take_home: Patients who started rehabilitation early after rotator cuff repair surgery had less stiffness and recovered shoulder function faster than those who delayed rehabilitation. However, this was an observational study so we cannot be certain early rehabilitation directly caused these improvements.

articles.title: Outcomes and Complications of Elbow Arthrodesis.
articles.authors: Clark SC, Diaw EF, Nieboer MJ, Morrey ME, Sanchez-Sotelo J
articles.population: Patients with severe elbow joint destruction not amenable to other surgical options, mostly posttraumatic arthritis
articles.sample_size: 13 elbows in 13 patients (11 male, 2 female, mean age 42 years)
articles.outcomes: Pain (VAS 2 at rest, 4 with activity), Mayo Elbow Performance Score (mean 49), SANE score (mean 46), satisfaction 8/10, 57% reported improvement. Complications in 46% including nonunion or fracture, 39% requiring revision surgery.
articles.take_home: Elbow arthrodesis provided reasonable pain relief and patient satisfaction, but had poor arm function and high complication rates (over 40% nonunion or fracture). It should only be considered as a last resort when other surgical options are not possible.

articles.title: Anxiety and depression are associated with increased complication risk after total elbow arthroplasty: A matched cohort study.
articles.authors: Smadi Z, Fiandeiro M, Pereira DE, Quaddoura A, Mozny A, Ilyas MH, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing total elbow arthroplasty between 2003 and 2023 with minimum two years follow-up
articles.sample_size: 2106 patients in each cohort after matching
articles.outcomes: 90-day complications including wound complications, anaemia, emergency department visits and readmission; two-year complications including mechanical loosening and dislocation
articles.take_home: Patients with both anxiety and depression who have total elbow arthroplasty experience more complications within 90 days and at two years compared to those without these conditions. These complications include wound problems, anaemia, hospital readmissions, and problems with the implant loosening or dislocating.

articles.title: Extensive metallosis following reverse shoulder arthroplasty managed with custom glenoid reconstruction: A case report.
articles.authors: Parmar T, Daher M, Fiandeiro M, Boufadel P, Fares M, Abboud JA
articles.population: Patient with reverse shoulder arthroplasty complications
articles.outcomes: Shoulder function, forward elevation, ability to perform activities of daily living
articles.take_home: A patient with severe metallosis and bone loss after reverse shoulder surgery required a two-stage revision using custom-made implants, which improved her shoulder function and movement at one year follow-up. This case shows that custom implants may be needed when standard revision options cannot provide stable fixation.

articles.title: Defining Long-Term Success After Anatomic Total Shoulder Arthroplasty: Survivorship and Clinically Important Outcomes.
articles.authors: Kucharik MP, Hung V, Jones T, Patel R, Ranson WA, Schmidt CM 2nd, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Implant survivorship at 10 and 15 years, American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons (ASES) scores, patient-acceptable symptom state (PASS), minimal clinically important difference (MCID), and substantial clinical benefit (SCB)
articles.take_home: Shoulder replacements had excellent survival rates of 96% at 10 years and 94% at 15 years, with most patients maintaining meaningful improvement in function, though shoulder function gradually declined over time. Younger patients and those with certain bone shapes (Walch B glenoid) had higher rates of needing revision surgery.

articles.title: Loss to Follow-up in Randomized Controlled Trials on Elbow Pathology: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Guven Z, de Klerk HH, Versteeg T, Priester-Vink S, Sierevelt IN, van den Bekerom MPJ
articles.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Patients with elbow pathology enrolled in randomised controlled trials with minimum six-month follow-up
articles.outcomes: Loss to follow-up rate and factors associated with loss to follow-up
articles.take_home: Research on elbow problems loses contact with an average of 12.1% of patients during follow-up. More frequent check-ins during the study appeared to help keep patients engaged, but most other factors like age, type of treatment, or how long the study lasted did not significantly affect dropout rates.

articles.title: Adoption of Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) and Trends in PROM Use in Shoulder Literature: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Alben MG, Frappa N, Chernov DV, Fucich D, Kalva SR, Yao JJ, et al.
articles.population: Shoulder orthopaedic research articles published 2015 to 2025
articles.sample_size: 3,473 articles met inclusion criteria from 7,416 reviewed
articles.outcomes: Adoption rates of PROMIS and other patient-reported outcome measures in shoulder orthopaedic studies; trends in PROM usage over time
articles.take_home: Although PROMIS is a standardised patient-centred tool, it remains rarely used in shoulder research, being adopted in only 3.3 per cent of studies with gradual increase from 0 per cent in 2015 to 5.5 per cent in 2025. Traditional outcome measures like the Constant score and Simple Shoulder Test remain more commonly used than PROMIS, though their use is declining.

articles.title: Biceps augmentation in dynamic anterior stabilization: A novel on-lay technique for challenging shoulder instabilities.
articles.authors: Silberberg J, Fernandez GH, Veramendi JLS
articles.population: Patients with anterior shoulder instability, subcritical glenoid bone loss, or poor anteroinferior capsulolabral tissue quality
articles.outcomes: Surgical technique combining biceps tendon transfer with glenoid rim fixation and supplementary augmentation
articles.take_home: This study describes a modified shoulder stabilisation surgery that uses the biceps tendon to reinforce repair in patients with severe tissue damage or bone loss, aiming to improve outcomes when standard repair alone may not be sufficient.

articles.title: The torque-angle relationship of shoulder rotator muscles: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Baptista de Oliveira Medeiros H, Campos Martins E, Neumann F, de Brito Fontana H
articles.population: Non-injured participants
articles.outcomes: Torque-angle relationship patterns of shoulder internal and external rotator muscles; peak torque positions; influence of joint position and testing methodology
articles.take_home: Shoulder rotator muscles produce peak torque near mid-range rotation angles, with external rotators showing descending or descending-then-rising patterns and internal rotators showing rising-then-falling patterns. However, current research is incomplete and varied in methods, so we need better studies to understand how these muscles work during real shoulder movements and in different populations.

articles.title: Age-related Humeral Retrotorsion Asymmetry in Junior Tennis Players: A Cross-sectional Ultrasound Study.
articles.authors: Numaguchi K, Momma D, Fukushima T, Munemori M, Matsui Y, Kondo E, et al.
articles.population: Competitive junior tennis players aged 9-17 years
articles.outcomes: Humeral retrotorsion angle measured in both shoulders using ultrasound; side-to-side difference between dominant and nondominant arms
articles.take_home: Junior tennis players develop a measurable difference in bone shape between their playing and non-playing shoulders from around age 10 onwards, with the playing arm having about 10 degrees more rotation. This is a normal adaptation to the repeated overhead movements of tennis.

articles.title: Does External Rotation Deficit After Arthroscopic Labral Repair with Remplissage Affect Clinically Meaningful Outcomes ?
articles.authors: Gungor CI, Oklaz EB, Akin B, Aral F, Ahmadov A, Somuncu D, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing arthroscopic labrum repair with remplissage for anterior shoulder instability
articles.outcomes: External rotation deficit, ASES score, WOSI score, VAS pain score, and achievement of MCID, SCB, and PASS thresholds
articles.take_home: Most patients achieved meaningful improvements in shoulder function and pain after surgery, with 71-93% reaching important outcome targets. Despite external rotation loss of 11-15 degrees occurring after surgery, this did not significantly affect patients' clinically meaningful results at two-year follow-up.

articles.title: Arthroscopic anterior shoulder bone-block stabilisation using distal clavicle autograft: A case series of 41 patients.
articles.authors: Kyriacou S, Little M, Elhoseiny A, Griffiths D, Baring T
articles.population: Patients with anterior shoulder instability and glenoid bone loss undergoing arthroscopic bone block stabilisation
articles.outcomes: Recurrent instability, Oxford Shoulder Instability Score, radiological union on CT scan, complications and donor site morbidity
articles.take_home: Arthroscopic shoulder stabilisation using distal clavicle bone graft was safe and effective, with 95% of patients showing good bone healing on scan and only one patient (2.4%) experiencing recurrent instability over an average 3-year follow-up. Patient-reported shoulder function improved significantly with no problems reported at the donor site where bone was taken from.

articles.title: Preoperative Malnutrition and Risk of Periprosthetic Joint Infection After Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty: Evaluation Using the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index.
articles.authors: Nishiura R, Nakazawa K, Manaka T, Hirakawa Y, Ito Y, Mori S, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Postoperative complications, periprosthetic joint infection, range of motion, pain scores, shoulder function scores, and minimal clinically important difference achievement at 2 years
articles.take_home: Patients with poor nutritional status before reverse shoulder replacement surgery had a higher risk of infection after the operation (10.4% versus 1.8%). Most other outcomes like movement and pain relief were similar between well-nourished and malnourished patients at 2 years.

articles.title: Acute Versus Chronic Essex-Lopresti Injuries: A Systematic Review of Management Strategies and Outcome Patterns.
articles.authors: Khan W, O'Neill A, Senthil A, Haque O, Bouchard MD, Nijjar M, et al.
articles.population: Patients with Essex-Lopresti injury (radial head fracture with interosseous membrane disruption and distal radioulnar joint instability)
articles.outcomes: Mayo Elbow Performance Score, Mayo Wrist Score, Disability of the Arm Shoulder and Hand score, complication rates, reoperation rates
articles.take_home: Patients treated early for Essex-Lopresti injury had better functional outcomes and fewer complications than those treated late, but all groups showed variable results with significant rates of complications and reoperations. The evidence is too mixed to recommend one best surgical approach.

articles.title: Proceedings from the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Orthopedic Infections: the definition of Shoulder Periprosthetic Joint infection.
articles.authors: Namdari S, Zmistowski B, Hsu J, Tashjian RZ, Nicholson T
articles.study_type: International consensus meeting using modified Delphi process and predictive statistical modelling
articles.population: International panel of shoulder surgeons and infectious disease specialists
articles.sample_size: 51 delegates; 86 systematic reviews analysed; data from American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons Multicenter Revision Arthroplasty and PJI Group dataset
articles.outcomes: Updated evidence-based definition of shoulder periprosthetic joint infection including major criteria, minor criteria, and diagnostic categories with statistical weighting
articles.take_home: Experts have agreed a new definition for shoulder joint infections after shoulder replacement, which simplifies diagnosis by removing organism virulence from consideration and uses weighted scoring of findings like blood tests, wound signs, and culture results to categorise infection likelihood.

articles.title: Biologic and Synthetic Augmentation in Rotator Cuff Repair: Emerging Technologies.
articles.authors: Boufadel P, Daher M, Satalich JR, Su F, Lindsay A, Khan AZ, et al.
articles.study_type: Literature review of rotator cuff repair augmentation technologies
articles.population: Patients with rotator cuff tears, particularly those with compromised tissue quality
articles.outcomes: Mechanical integrity of repairs, biologic healing at tendon-bone interface, structural healing, retear rates
articles.take_home: Bioinductive collagen implants show the strongest evidence for improving rotator cuff repair healing and reducing retear rates in selected patients. Xenografts are no longer recommended due to poor outcomes, whilst allografts, synthetic grafts, and biceps tendon autografts may help in some cases, though more research is needed.
